articles.title: Oblak: "Me da igual el Clásico... La Liga es muy larga y hay que pensar en nosotros"
articles.standfirst: El meta esloveno atendió a los medios a la conclusión del 1-0 ante el Deportivo.
articles.summary: El meta esloveno atendió a los medios a la conclusión del 1-0 ante el Deportivo.
articles.body: Oblak atendió a los medios a la conclusión de un partido en el que volvió a ser decisivo con varias paradas de mérito. Resumen partido: "Nos ha costado mucho. No hemos estado del todo bien. Primera parte bastante mal. Segunda mejor, subimos ritmo, pero luego bajamos un poco otra vez. El Deportivo es muy buen equipo y te puede castigar. Tuvimos un poquito de suerte. Menos mal que no nos castigaron y nos llevamos los tres puntos". Plan: "Nos costaba mucho robar. No era el plan de partido. Nos ha costado físicamente, parece que no nos hemos activado desde el inicio. Muchas veces los partidos se pierden en las primeras partes. Era algo que habíamos mejorado pero hoy volvimos a bajar el ritmo. Si lo bajas es imposible. Hay que estar al 200%". Gol de Julián: "Está claro que Julián es muy importante, que marque Julián. Está dando lo máximo de sí mismo. Feliz por él. Estoy seguro que poco a poco se ganará a la gente otra vez. Es un gran jugador, ya lo ha demostrado y está claro que lo necesitamos en la mejor forma posible". El Clásico: "Me da igual el Clásico. La Liga es muy larga y hay que pensar en nosotros. No podemos perder puntos. Ellos son dos grandes equipos. Nosotros estar arriba y pelear hasta el final. Ojalá se pueda hacer".

articles.title: No. 19 Texas blows 21-point halftime lead but still does enough to beat No. 7 Ole Miss
articles.summary: Arch Manning scored two rushing touchdowns and threw for another but also had three turnovers.
articles.body:
No. 19 Texas coughed up a 21-point lead but did enough in the fourth quarter to take down No. 7 Ole Miss 34-27.

The Longhorns led 24-3 at halftime and proceeded to give up 21 straight points as Ole Miss tied the game. Arch Manning's short touchdown run with 8:04 to go put the Longhorns ahead for good before a curious tactical decision hurt Ole Miss' chances of winning the game.

But the Rebels still somehow had a shot to at least tie the game in the final minutes.

After kicking a field goal to cut Texas' lead to seven inside the final two minutes, the Rebels needed to recover an onside kick. And they did after the kick bounced off multiple players.

But without any timeouts, Ole Miss ran out of time. The Rebels got to the Texas 24-yard line, but Trinidad Chambliss' last-gasp pass was intercepted in the end zone.

After Manning gave Texas a 31-24 lead, Ole Miss started with the ball on its own 47-yard line after a late hit penalty on the ensuing kickoff return. The Rebels gained just 12 yards and faced fourth-and-10 from the Texas 41-yard line while trailing by seven.

A field goal would simply cut Texas' lead to four with just over six minutes to go. The Rebels would still need to find the end zone or kick two more field goals to take the lead. And yet, Ole Miss coach Pete Golding sent out Lucas Carneiro for a 58-yard field goal attempt.

The play clock was winding down as the strong-legged Carneiro lined up for the kick. Instead of taking a delay of game and punting — a defensible decision given the game context — Golding called his first timeout. He then kept Carneiro on the field to try to cut the lead to four.

Texas then drained nearly four minutes off the clock before Gianni Spetic's short field goal made it a two-possession lead that Ole Miss ultimately couldn't overcome.

Another uneven performance for the Texas offense

Texas is still looking to put a complete game together.

The Longhorns looked like the preseason top-five team they were billed as in the first half as they scored three straight touchdowns to build that 24-3 lead. The Longhorns were dominant in the second quarter, as Manning found Ryan Wingo for a 50-yard TD after he ran for his first score.

But Manning also turned the ball over three times. With starting left tackle Trevor Goosby carted off in the first half and unavailable, Manning fumbled on the first drive of the third quarter after instant pressure off the left side. That fumble was recovered by Kam Franklin in the end zone for an Ole Miss touchdown.

Texas then punted three straight times as Ole Miss tied the game and Manning threw his second pick of the game on a horrible decision into triple coverage early in the fourth quarter.

It was a play that could have been costly. Instead, the Texas defense quickly forced a punt, and the Longhorns drove 80 yards in six plays for Manning's go-ahead touchdown.

That drive was powered by running back Raleek Brown, who shouldered much of the rushing workload with Hollywood Smothers sidelined by a shoulder injury. Brown finished the game with 23 carries for 157 yards.

There are still five weeks of the regular season to go. But if the season ended today, Georgia would face Kentucky in the SEC championship game.

The Bulldogs and Wildcats are the only two teams in the SEC with just one conference loss through Week 8. Thanks to Texas' win, eight teams currently have two league losses, while another four have three losses.

Georgia and Kentucky don't play each other in 2026, though both have three ranked teams still remaining on their conference schedules. We're confident in saying that one or both of the league's title game participants is going to have two conference losses.

We have no idea who those teams will be, however. Though one thing is for certain: tiebreakers are going to be in play.

articles.title: Rodri, de deseo blanco a líder culé
articles.standfirst: Rechazó en verano al bloque de Mourinho para firmar por el conjunto culé
articles.summary: Rechazó en verano al bloque de Mourinho para firmar por el conjunto culé
articles.body: Uno de los grandes nombres propios del pasado mercado de verano fue el de Rodri. Cuando surgió la posibilidad de que el centrocampista abandonara el Manchester City, tanto el Real Madrid como el Barcelona dieron un paso al frente. El conjunto blanco necesitaba reforzar su medular y el equipo azulgrana, por su parte, aunque parecía tener bien cubierta esa demarcación sobre el papel, no quería dejar escapar la oportunidad de incorporar a uno de los mejores centrocampistas del mundo. El Real Madrid apostó con fuerza por su fichaje. Mantuvieron varios contactos con el jugador para tratar de convencerlo de que su futuro debía pasar por el Bernabéu. Incluso Mourinho intervino para intentar inclinar la balanza a favor del conjunto blanco. La operación se convirtió así en uno de los grandes focos de atención del mercado estival. Sin embargo, Rodri terminó decantándose por el Barcelona. El internacional explicó que su decisión respondía fundamentalmente a cuestiones futbolísticas: dónde podía seguir creciendo como jugador, qué proyecto le ofrecía mayores posibilidades de desarrollo, la posibilidad de liderar a un vestuario con una importante presencia de jóvenes... La decisión estuvo vinculada, por encima de todo, a su visión del proyecto deportivo. Ahora, dos meses después de aquella elección y de su llegada al conjunto azulgrana, el centrocampista se prepara para reencontrarse con el equipo al que rechazó durante el verano. En el Barcelona, Rodri se ha convertido en un futbolista imprescindible, en un líder. Ha sido titular en ocho de los nueve últimos compromisos del conjunto azulgrana. Y resulta especialmente llamativo que su única suplencia en ese periodo se produjera contra el PSG el martes, precisamente en el último compromiso que ha perdido el conjunto de Flick. Rodri saltó al terreno de juego durante la última media hora. Rodri ofrece salida de balón, facilita la circulación y ayuda a controlar los tiempos del partido. Su tándem con Pedri permite al conjunto azulgrana presumir de tener uno de los mejores centros del campo del mundo.

articles.title: FIFA U15 World Cup 2026: India beat Cameroon 2-1, register second consecutive Group K win
articles.summary: India continued their impressive start at the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup 2026, beating Cameroon 2-1 in their second Group K match on Sunday.
articles.body: India continued their impressive start at the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup 2026, beating Cameroon 2-1 in their second Group K match on Sunday. The Blue Colts took an early lead through a Cameroon own goal, but Muhammad Sohil Khan’s own goal brought the African side level before the break.Captain R Lalremruatfela scored the winner in the second half, finishing a low cross from Deepak Singh Arambam. Goalkeeper Jenit Ningthoujam played a key role in the victory, making several important saves, including stopping a penalty.With two wins from two matches, India are the only team in Group K to have won both their games so far.Jenit shines as India withstand Cameroon pressureIndia got off to a quick start in rainy conditions when Deepak’s corner in the first minute led to Fareil Ngobo accidentally putting the ball into his own net. Cameroon gradually grew into the game, but India defended well and created chances to extend their lead.Goalkeeper Jenit was particularly impressive, denying several Cameroon attempts, including a dangerous free-kick and a close-range effort. India also came close to scoring through Lalremruatfela, but Cameroon managed to clear the danger.Cameroon eventually equalised in the 20th minute when Ndam Moctar’s cross struck Muhammad Sohil Khan and went into the net. The teams went into the break level at 1-1.Lalremruatfela scores winner as Jenit saves penaltyIndia came out with greater purpose after half-time, and substitute Ronandev Aheibam made an immediate impact by winning the ball in midfield. He passed it wide to Deepak, who sent a low cross into the box. Lalremruatfela calmly finished with his left foot in the 27th minute to put India back in front.Cameroon had a chance to equalise after being awarded a penalty for handball, but Jenit came to India’s rescue once again, saving Harouna Abdoulaye’s spot-kick in the 32nd minute.India continued to threaten, with Ronandev testing the Cameroon goalkeeper and Soumojit Sarkar forcing another save from a free-kick. The Blue Colts held their lead until the final whistle, securing their second consecutive win and strengthening their position in Group K.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: What have Manchester United changed to turn around their WSL form?
articles.summary: It's a different picture at Manchester United now than it was last month - so what have they changed to turn around their WSL form?
articles.body:
It is a different picture at Manchester United now than it was last month as they gear up for the derby against Women's Super League leaders Manchester City.

Eva Olid's side were without a win and low on confidence after their opening three matches in a disappointing start to the season.

But after getting their first win on the board against Sheffield United in the Women's League Cup, United have won six successive matches in all competitions.

They now sit fifth in the table, eight points off unbeaten rivals City, who they face on Sunday (18:00 GMT) hoping to continue their positive form.

So what has changed at United to overturn their fortunes?

Listen to BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra commentary and follow live text updates on the BBC Sport website

The most noticeable changes have happened on the pitch as new manager Olid, who joined in the summer, conceded her side needed to revert to old ways.

They were struggling to adapt to her new style which demands lots of possession, an attacking mindset and high-risk football.

They struggled in defeats by London City Lionesses and Chelsea, having just two shots on target and less than 40% possession in both matches.

Olid felt her team were trying to do too much and had lost sight of some of their strengths, including their defensive organisation.

She urged her players to revert to what they knew before their 1-1 draw with Arsenal, which showed signs of improvement.

"The things they were good at before, they need to keep and at the same time, little by little, we need to implement our new style," Olid said before that game.

"It's trying to find this balance. Maybe they thought I would expect them to do everything in the first match but that is impossible. You need time."

That draw at Emirates Stadium was the catalyst for change at United, offering a foundation to build upon.

They had a tough start but then had a run of games against lower-ranked opposition, and two successive WSL matches at home.

The difference from their first three WSL games and their next three was stark.

They won the maximum nine points, scored six goals, conceded just two and almost doubled their possession percentage.

By returning to a more familiar defensive structure and adding in elements of Olid's new style, they began to cause more problems up front too.

Having had just 197 passes ending in the final third in their first three games, they recorded a combined 529 against West Ham, Liverpool and Charlton Athletic.

They quadrupled the number of shots they took too, going from 10 to 42 and won more duels in the air.

Perhaps the biggest changes at United have been off the pitch.

Olid explained that her side had navigated a "transitional period" and had taken part in big discussions following their 5-0 drubbing by Chelsea.

Players needed to find confidence and Olid admitted the "honest conversations" had to come up with a solution.

"The first two games were good learning for us to connect as a team and for me to know what the players needed from me," said Olid. "The players also know what I needed. It was about trying to find that balance.

"I feel now we are connected. That doesn't mean we won't have more [of those] less good days, but I think we have that understanding of each other."

Their form at the start of the season impacted individuals with vice-captain Ella Toone missing out on England selection for the first time under Sarina Wiegman.

She responded by scoring in their 3-1 win at Charlton on Sunday, while summer signing Andrea Medina has grown to become a crucial member of the squad.

The international break proved to be a valuable time for Olid to readjust to her new role, reflect on what needed to change and to spend time on the training pitch.

England defender and United captain Maya le Tissier was among those to return with renewed energy having impressed for her country during the break.

The backroom staff positions were also confirmed and Olid has been able to build a group she hopes can lead United to success going forward.

Fellow Spaniard Jose Herrera joined as assistant coach, alongside Gavin Beith, who worked with Olid at former club Hearts.

Speaking about the international break, Olid said: "I had time to re-organise everything, the roles for the new staff and how we are going to work together.

"This break, for me, was amazing. It was like a new start. It was about keeping the good energy from the last matches but then having a new start."

Now, having been on a winning run, Olid hopes the proposition of a Manchester derby on Sunday will prove to be added motivation for her players.

"I always think that before big games, you want to give confidence to the players and at the same time, you try to motivate them with the opposition," she told BBC.

"It's a derby. I think the players are always motivated, but against City, there has to be something else, no?"

articles.title: Neymar, tras su expulsión: "Le di la oportunidad a un idiota de hacerse notar"
articles.standfirst: El brasileño vio la roja por taparse la boca al hablar con Rodrigo Nestor, del Bahía: "Es una ley creada contra el racismo, y él quiso aprovecharse de ella"
articles.summary: El brasileño vio la roja por taparse la boca al hablar con Rodrigo Nestor, del Bahía: "Es una ley creada contra el racismo, y él quiso aprovecharse de ella"
articles.body: Neymar habló después del partido entre el Santos y el Bahía donde fue expulsado por taparse la boca cuando se dirigía a Rodrigo Nestor. El brasileño fue muy crítico con el jugador rival y pidió disculpas a su afición. "No soy muy de hablar sobre lo que pasa en el partido, pero lo que hizo Nestor conmigo es muy grave. Grave porque es una ley creada contra el racismo, y él quiso aprovecharse de ella", comentó en su Instagram. "Estoy muy triste, porque él fue muy safado (deshonesto). Muy safado, de verdad. Dijo en la entrevista que no podía repetir lo que yo dije, porque hay niños viendo... Hermano, él simuló. Yo tiré el balón a su cintura y él se llevó la mano a la cara. ¿Qué ejemplo quiere dar? Habló de educación... Hermano, yo también tengo educación. Y otra cosa: yo soy hombre", comentaba Neymar. "Lo que hiciste no se hace. Y quien creó esa ley, cuidado. Porque puede haber safadeza (desfachatez) y pasar lo que me pasó a mí. Hice una mierda, ¿no? Le di oportunidad a un idiota de hacerse notar. Gracias, Nestor, yo voy a dormir con la conciencia tranquila. Tú, con tu safadeza, no vas a dormir tranquilo, no. No vas a dormir tranquilo, no!", concluyó.

images.caption: Neymar en un partido con el Santos. Guilherme Dionizio

articles.title: A qué hora es el Real Sociedad - Levante: horario, dónde ver en TV y canal del partido de LaLiga EA Sports
articles.standfirst: Partidazo en Anoeta entre dos equipos al alza
articles.summary: Partidazo en Anoeta entre dos equipos al alza
articles.body: La Real Sociedad recibirá esta tarde al Levante en Anoeta con la intención de sumar su cuarta victoria seguida en LaLiga y mantenerse en los puestos europeos, a los que soñarán con acercarse los granotas, algo que podrían hacer si dan continuidad al triunfo del miércoles contra el Athletic y se llevan los tres puntos. Ambos equipos están protagonizando partidos con goles, así que todo apunta a tarde entretenida. El partido entre Real Sociedad y Levante de la jornada 10 de LaLiga EA Sports se juega el domingo 25 de octubre a las 18:30 horas. El partido entre Real Sociedad y Levante de la jornada 10 de LaLiga EA Sports se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través del canal DAZN LaLiga. También se podrá seguir el partido a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y con los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde dos horas antes, sigue la previa y los onces. Tras el encuentro, podrás leer la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas y ver el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles. La Real Sociedad llega tras haber sumado tres victorias consecutivas en LaLiga EA Sports, la última ante el Málaga por 2-5 en el Estadio La Rosaleda. El Levante llega tras haber ganado al Athletic Club entre semana. Era el partido aplazado de la jornada 6 y los granotas se llevaron los tres puntos ganando 3-1 a los rojiblancos.

articles.title: Mourinho contra el mejor Barça de la historia: tres años de guerra en 17 batallas
articles.standfirst: De la goleada del 5-0 al dedo en el ojo de Tito Vilanova, del “¿por qué?” al “calma” de Cristiano: la crónica de la rivalidad más tensa que ha vivido el fútbol español, cuando el portugués se midió al Barça de Guardiola
articles.summary: De la goleada del 5-0 al dedo en el ojo de Tito Vilanova, del “¿por qué?” al “calma” de Cristiano: la crónica de la rivalidad más tensa que ha vivido el fútbol español, cuando el portugués se midió al Barça de Guardiola
articles.body: Pocas veces el fútbol ha sido tan parecido a una trinchera. Entre noviembre de 2010 y marzo de 2013, José Mourinho y el Barcelona libraron 17 Clásicos que no se jugaban solo en el césped, sino en las salas de prensa, en los despachos de la UEFA y en el imaginario de dos aficiones que aprendieron a tenerse manía con método. Enfrente tenía el portugués a uno de los mejores equipos que ha pisado un campo en este siglo, aquel Barça de Guardiola. Mourinho no vino a admirarlo; vino a derribarlo, y para ello estaba dispuesto a ensuciarse las manos. El prólogo lo había escrito él mismo meses antes, cuando su Inter eliminó a ese Barça en una semifinal de Champions y celebró el pase corriendo bajo los aspersores del Camp Nou. Aquella carrera fue su carta de presentación en una ciudad que ya conocía: Mourinho había sido allí traductor y ayudante de Robson y Van Gaal en los noventa, un segundo de a bordo que volvía convertido en almirante del enemigo. El primer acto fue una bofetada. El 29 de noviembre de 2010, en su estreno como visitante en el Camp Nou, el Madrid encajó un 5-0 que todavía duele en Concha Espina. Mourinho, que jamás en su carrera había recibido cinco goles, salió a la sala de prensa sin esconderse: “Es una derrota muy fácil de digerir. Premia a un equipo que jugó muy bien y castiga a otro que jugó muy mal”. Piqué despidió a los blancos enseñando los cinco dedos de la manita. Fue la última vez que el portugués aceptó una derrota con deportividad. A partir de ahí, cambió de armas. La primavera de 2011 marcó un antes y un después. En apenas dieciocho días, Madrid y Barça se vieron cuatro veces: Liga, final de Copa y la ida y vuelta de las semifinales de Champions. El Madrid rescató la Copa en Mestalla, con un cabezazo de Cristiano en la prórroga que rompió una sequía de dieciocho años, pero el fútbol pronto quedó sepultado bajo la pólvora dialéctica. En la previa de la Champions, Guardiola, harto, estalló con una frase que resume una época: “En esta sala, él es el puto jefe, el puto amo. Fuera del campo ya me ha ganado. No quiero competir ni un instante”. Uno de los técnicos más elegante del mundo bajaba al barro al que Mourinho lo había arrastrado. Después vino el monólogo más célebre de la carrera del portugués. Tras caer 0-2 en el Bernabéu, con Pepe expulsado y él mismo enviado a la grada, Mourinho convirtió la rueda de prensa en un juicio sumarísimo: “¿Por qué? ¿Por qué? ¿Por qué?”, repitió, antes de enumerar árbitros como quien recita una lista negra y de dejar una sentencia envenenada: “Guardiola es un fantástico entrenador, pero ha ganado una Champions que a mí me daría vergüenza ganar”. La UEFA lo sancionó con cinco partidos. El Barça pasó a Wembley y levantó la Orejona. Mourinho había perdido la batalla deportiva, pero había plantado una semilla de sospecha que germinaría durante años. En la Supercopa de agosto de 2011, una tangana en el descuento del Camp Nou terminó con la imagen que lo persigue para siempre: Mourinho acercándose por la espalda al banquillo rival y metiéndole el dedo en el ojo a Tito Vilanova, el segundo de Guardiola. Interrogado después, no solo negó la agresión, sino que humilló a su víctima: “¿Pito Vilanova? No sé quién es ese Pito”. Piqué resumió el sentir de media España: “Mourinho está destrozando el fútbol español”. El dedo en el ojo fue mucho más que un gesto, fue el símbolo de una rivalidad que había perdido los frenos. Y sin embargo, en mitad del fango, germinó el fútbol. La temporada 2011-12 trajo el Clásico más importante de aquellos tres años. El 21 de abril de 2012, en un Camp Nou abarrotado, Cristiano recibió de Ozil, batió a Valdés y mandó callar a noventa mil almas con las palmas hacia abajo: “Calma”. Aquel 1-2 encarriló la única Liga que el Madrid le arrebató a aquel Barça, un título de récord con cien puntos que puso fin a la hegemonía culé. Seis días después, agotado, Guardiola anunció que se marchaba. Mourinho había conseguido su propósito: desgastar al coloso hasta que el coloso dijo basta. El tercer acto fue la redención, aunque con sabor agridulce. Con Guardiola fuera y un Tito Vilanova que pronto tendría que ausentarse para tratarse un cáncer, la balanza se inclinó por fin del lado blanco. Mourinho ganó la Supercopa de 2012 y, ya en 2013, eliminó al Barça en las semifinales de Copa con un contundente 1-3 en el Camp Nou. Cerró su serie particular con cinco Clásicos seguidos sin perder, como si el tiempo quisiera concederle una tregua antes de la despedida. El portugués, que había empezado recibiendo cinco goles, se iba dándole lecciones a su verdugo. El balance de aquellos tres años es un empate técnico que esconde una guerra total: cinco victorias, seis empates y seis derrotas. Pero reducir aquello a números sería traicionar su esencia. Mourinho no transformó solo un marcador. Transformó la manera de entender el Clásico, lo convirtió en un campo de batalla psicológico del que el fútbol español tardó años en recuperarse. Quien quiera entender el Clásico de hoy, con sus mosaicos, sus pancartas y sus recelos arbitrales, haría bien en mirar atrás. Allí, en aquellas diecisiete batallas, está el origen de casi todo.

articles.title: 75 veces al rescate
articles.standfirst: Lunin cumple su efemérides en el Madrid siempre de urgencia en sus siete años de blanco
articles.summary: Lunin cumple su efemérides en el Madrid siempre de urgencia en sus siete años de blanco
articles.body: En los matrimonios cumplir 75 años es la Boda de Brillantes; en el caso de Andriy Lunin, que se casó en chándal, más le vale brillar porque es la 75ª vez que acude al rescate de la portería blanca de urgencia, siempre resguardada por Courtois, sobre el que no hay debate. Siempre se le requiere de un día para otro, vive en un susto permanente. Habitual bombero en el Madrid, aterriza de nuevo sin un solo minuto esta temporada ni en Liga ni en Champions. Su último partido en Liga fue en ante el Espanyol en mayo aunque había vuelto a la titularidad contra el Atleti también por lesión del belga. Y la última en Champions en abril en la derrota 4-3 en Múnich, hace casi medio año. No tiene partidos pequeños el chico. Eso sí todos los aficionados blancos recuerdan su memorable temporada en 2024, llevando en volandas al equipo hasta la decimoquinta contra el Dortmund en Wembley, con grandes actuaciones ante City (con tanda de penaltis para la historia) o Bayern. Luego en la de 2026 no anduvo tan fino también contra el equipo muniqués. En los 74 anteriores ha recibido 91 goles (23 partidos imbatido), 3 amarillas y 1 roja en todas las competiciones. En este Real Madrid del regreso de Mourinho, Lunin ha arrancado su séptima temporada a la sombra de Courtois. El belga, que se cae esta noche por una gripe inoportuna, ya forma parte de la historia de la portería blanca. Para muchos, el guardameta más grande de la historia del club, por encima de Casillas, Zamora, Araquistain... Un dominio de su puesto que no admite debate alguno y que apenas encuentra puntos débiles en su primera temporada en la Casa Blanca: en la 2018-19. El portero ucraniano, después de un par de años de cesiones, se instaló en la primera plantilla del Madrid en el verano de 2020, el de la pandemia. A esas alturas, Courtois ya era intocable para Zidane. Como luego lo fue para Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso, Arbeloa y, ahora, Mourinho. En ese recorrido de portero suplente de largo aliento apareció un oasis: la temporada 2023-24. La grave lesión de rodilla que sufrió Courtois a las puertas de LaLiga llevó al club a fichar a Kepa. Parecía una condena a otra suplencia para el ucraniano. Sin embargo, tras la Supercopa de España, Lunin se convirtió en el titular y en el héroe del Madrid en la tanda de penaltis del Etihad. Eso sí, en cuanto Courtois estuvo listo para regresar, Ancelotti volvió a darle las llaves de la portería. Suya fue la final de la Champions en Wembley. Lunin afronta la temporada con el mismo papel de las anteriores: a la sombra de Courtois y a la espera de que Mourinho le conceda oportunidades en la Copa más allá de la de esta noche. La temporada pasada apenas disputó el partido de Albacete hasta que las lesiones se cruzaron en el camino del guardameta belga y le abrieron las puertas de la titularidad. Así, el portero de Krasnohrad sumó seis apariciones en LaLiga. La falta de minutos en el Real Madrid ha provocado que Lunin desaparezca de las convocatorias de la selección ucraniana. No porque la titularidad de Trubin, el guardameta del Benfica, sea intocable, sino porque Ucrania no cuenta con el portero de Krasnohrad desde junio de 2025. Y se trata de una situación que, por ahora, parece no tener fácil solución. A la espera de aumentar su número de partidos con el Real Madrid, Lunin suma 74 encuentros defendiendo la portería blanca en las seis temporadas que lleva en el club. En ese recorrido ha conquistado once títulos, entre ellos dos Ligas de Campeones. Un currículo de gran nivel, muy por encima del que han firmado otros guardametas suplentes en la historia de la entidad de Chamartín.

articles.title: Uli Hoeneß: Florian Wirtz would play 'much better' for Bayern than at Liverpool
articles.summary: Uli Hoeneß believes Florian Wirtz would play 'much better' for Bayern Munich than he currently does at Liverpool.The Bayern honorary president made the remar...
articles.body:
Uli Hoeneß believes Florian Wirtz would play 'much better' for Bayern Munich than he currently does at Liverpool .

The Bayern honorary president made the remarks in an interview with German newspaper Welt am Sonntag.

Wirtz made his name at Bayer Leverkusen before moving to Anfield, in a then-British record deal worth up to £116m. He arrived in England as a back-to-back winner of the Bundesliga 's Player of the Season award, but the 23-year-old has not hit the heights expected.

Hoeneß has been keeping a close eye on the German's fortunes and his verdict is that the problem lies in how Liverpool have used him.

Hoeneß contrasted Wirtz's central role at Leverkusen with his standing in the Liverpool side, suggesting he has lost the influence that made him stand out in the Bundesliga.

Bayern Munich had been interested in signing Wirtz prior to his Premier League transfer, and Hoeneß is confident the environment at the Allianz Arena would suit the midfielder more.

Hoeneß questions Liverpool's use of Wirtz: "In Leverkusen, he got every ball"

"Florian Wirtz would play much better for Bayern than he does at Liverpool," Hoeneß told Welt am Sonntag .

"I watch a lot of his games. They haven't integrated him properly at all. In Leverkusen, he got every ball; in Liverpool, he's just one among many."

Wirtz has faced scrutiny after a slow start to his second season at Liverpool, and was singled out after the 3-0 defeat to Manchester City earlier this month.

However, he has shown glimpses of improvement in recent games. The Germany international has recorded goal involvements in each of his last three appearances, and opened his goal account against Villarreal in midweek.

Liverpool take on Brighton in the Premier League this afternoon, with Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler discussing Wirtz ahead of the game. He said the Seagulls must stop Wirtz's impact as a collective, highlighting his ability in one-vs-one situations.

articles.title: Barcelona revive interest in €30m-rated Juventus defender; move dependent on Alejandro Balde – report
articles.summary: Barcelona made quite a few signings during the summer transfer window, bringing in the likes of Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Rodri and Joao Cancelo.One oth...
articles.body:
Barcelona made quite a few signings during the summer transfer window, bringing in the likes of Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Rodri and Joao Cancelo.

One other player the Catalan club were interested in but eventually did not move for was Juventus full-back Andrea Cambiaso.

Now, according to Calciomercato (h/t FCB World ), Barça have renewed their interest in the versatile full-back.

The Catalans are monitoring the Italy international, who could become a serious option if someone like Alejandro Balde leaves Hansi Flick's squad.

Juventus set €30 million asking price for Cambiaso

The Italian giants value Cambiaso at around €30 million, with the defender under contract until June 2029.

His ability to operate on either flank makes him an attractive option for Barcelona, particularly given Flick's preference for versatile defenders comfortable in possession.

Andrea Cambiaso is a fullback on Barcelona's radar. (Photo by Chris Ricco/Getty Images)

Cambiaso has endured a difficult start to the new season, suffering from an ankle problem that has limited his involvement at Juventus.

Meanwhile, Barça potentially making a move for Cambiaso could depend directly on the future of out-of-favour Alejandro Balde.

Roma are considering a January loan move for the Spaniard with an option to buy, while Juventus have also previously shown interest in his services.

That said, there have been no formal negotiations between the two clubs so far for either full-back.

Would Cambiaso be a sensible replacement for Balde?

Cambiaso's versatility is the most exciting aspect of his profile, and he could provide squad depth on both flanks.

His attacking instincts and willingness to advance into forward areas, whether overlapping or inverting into midfield, would suit Barça 's approach.

Nevertheless, spending €30 million on another full-back would be justified only if Barça managed to recoup a similar amount or more from a sale like Balde's.

Hansi Flick already has Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart, who can play on both flanks, and should not add another name for the sake of it.

Barcelona need to make a decision on the development of Alejandro Balde. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images)

Balde's situation is equally serious . Although the academy graduate has struggled for minutes, he remains a young player with considerable pace and attacking potential.

Allowing him to leave on loan without a purchase option would be a much better option than parting ways with him permanently.

Barça should therefore assess whether signing Cambiaso would genuinely improve the squad or if they would be better off trusting Balde.

It remains to be seen how Cambiaso recovers from his ankle problem and whether Barcelona make a move for him in the near future.

articles.title: Australia reach World Cup semis & New Zealand get back on track
articles.summary: Australia edge to a 36-22 victory in a pulsating Group A match against Fiji to book their place in the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals.
articles.body:
Australia edged to a 36-22 victory in a pulsating match against Fiji to book their place in the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals.

Having lost their previous five meetings against Australia by an aggregate score of 246-16, a stunned Brisbane crowd watched Fiji enjoy territorial advantage in the first half and take a 16-12 lead after the break.

However, the momentum switched back to Kevin Walters' side in a crucial 60-second spell.

Solomone Saukuru raced in to seemingly put Fiji 20-12 ahead - but when it was ruled out for obstruction, Australia immediately went up the other end and Tom Trbojevic scored to bring the teams level.

Trbojevic, who looked vulnerable in defence, crossed twice more for Australia and Jacob Preston added a further try after Semi Valemei had completed his hat-trick for Fiji.

"There are definitely some areas to improve on," Trbojevic told Premier Sports. "We didn't start as we wanted to and couldn't get a flow. We just needed to play our style of footy.

"We weren't at our best but we came away with two points. We need to improve. We've got to enjoy a win but we've got to be our harshest critics too."

Brisbane Broncos centre Kotoni Staggs had opened the scoring for Australia on his home ground, while Sam Walker capped his debut with a try and 12 points with the boot.

But the manner in which their pack were outmuscled - and in which they allowed Taane Milne and Valemei to score - will be a concern for Walters, whose team head into the last four despite delivering two unconvincing performances in beating New Zealand and Fiji.

New Zealand will take on Fiji in a make-or-break final pool game on Saturday, 31 October (04:30 GMT), having overcome an early scare themselves in their 82-16 victory over the Cook Islands in Christchurch.

Jamayne Isaako, who is joining Melbourne Storm next term, took the headlines as he scored a record 38 points for the Kiwis.

It was the perfect way for Stacey Jones' team to bounce back from their 24-22 opening Group A defeat by Australia but it did not go entirely to script, as the Cook Islands recovered from 12-0 down to lead 16-12.

With two-time World Cup winner Valentine Holmes in their ranks, Karmichael Hunt's team responded superbly as Esom Ioka grabbed a hat-trick of tries in response to early efforts from Isaako and Ronaldo Mulitalo.

However, from there it was one-way traffic as the Kiwis took control to lead 36-16 by the break.

Isaako crossed three times overall, while Test debutant Tanner Stowers-Smith, Mulitalo and Casey McLean each scored twice.

Scott Sorensen, Kodi Nikorima, Te Maire Martin, Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad and Keano Kini, who replaced injured star full-back Kalyn Ponga in the New Zealand line-up, also claimed tries.

Isaako's points haul - which included 13 conversions - eclipsed Tasesa Lavea's previous mark of 32 points in a single game, which was recorded against the same opposition in 2000.

Kiwi Ferns roll towards Samoa or England clash

New Zealand's women had earlier thrashed France 92-0 in the same stadium, with Apii Nicholls scoring four tries.

Stacey Waaka and Mele Hufanga both claimed a hat-trick of tries in a dominant performance by the co-hosts.

Mackenzie Wiki, Raecene McGregor and Tenika Willison all crossed twice with Chantay Kiria-Ratu and Kaiyah Atai also going over in an 18-try demolition job.

The Kiwi Ferns have now defeated France by a combined score of 236-0 across three World Cup encounters.

New Zealand, who defeated Fiji 18-12 in the their opening match, will round off their Pool B campaign against Papua New Guinea on Saturday, 31 October (06:45 GMT).

Ricky Henry's side look set to face either Samoa or England in the semi-finals of the competition.

Fiji face France in the other remaining group match on Saturday, 31 October (02:20 GMT).

images.caption: Jamayne Isaako eclipsed Tasesa Lavea's points record set in 2000 [Getty Images]
Raecene McGregor laid on five tries and scored two herself for New Zealand [Getty Images]

articles.title: Cesc Fabregas hails Como’s squad depth as they follow up historic Man Utd clash with crucial Sassuolo win
articles.summary: Cesc Fabregas has lauded the growing maturity of his Como side after they successfully navigated a grueling schedule to secure a 2-0 victory against Sassuolo...
articles.body:
Cesc Fabregas has lauded the growing maturity of his Como side after they successfully navigated a grueling schedule to secure a 2-0 victory against Sassuolo. Following their historic European exploits against Manchester United, the Italian outfit proved they have the depth to compete on multiple fronts.

Como continued their impressive run of form on Saturday, securing a third consecutive victory with a professional 2-0 win over Sassuolo. A brace from Tasos Douvikas was enough to seal the points, but the real story for Fabregas was his team's ability to maintain high energy levels despite a congested fixture list that recently included a high-profile Champions League encounter with Manchester United .

"It depends. Every time is a bit different, today certainly it was more the physical aspect, the games against Manchester United and Fiorentina before took energy away from us," Fabregas explained, as quoted by TUTTOmercatoWEB . "Coming to compete here... it mattered to arrive with energy. With people who had been waiting for weeks or months to find space. The real challenge of this season is the close games. The biggest teams, if you see, are in difficulty with so many changes."

The former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder emphasized the importance of his fringe players stepping up when called upon. "The other team instead arrives after 8 days of preparing for the match. Victory gives you extra strength, even better to win in this way. Today Kambwala played, Ricci, Lahdo made his debut. Having everyone available and giving a hand until the end of the season is a good thing," he added.

Greek forward Douvikas was the undisputed star of the show, and Fabregas was quick to point out the immense work rate behind the striker's clinical finishing. The Spaniard believes Douvikas has all the attributes required to become one of the most feared center-forwards in the division if he continues his current trajectory of development.

"Tasos wants you to give him information. He always wants to talk, he is a guy who always wants to improve, he is scoring goals... I know how much work is behind it. He is growing in a way that could make him become a very, very important center-forward. He trains at a thousand, he is a very generous guy, in this sense we are very happy. In these last three years, he has been one of those signings that has given satisfaction," he noted.

Beyond the attacking displays, Como's defensive resilience caught the eye as they kept a clean sheet despite fielding a brand-new backline. Fabregas noted that the team is becoming more adept at managing different phases of the game, a skill they have refined even since their testing night against Manchester United at Old Trafford.

"I am very happy with this. When a team defends well it is always better than attacking. We must gain confidence. Even after Manchester United it seems that the team is managing some aspects to improve better. If you look at the defense today it is the first time they have all played together. Plus Ricci in front of them. We cannot forget this and I don't. There is work behind it. The guys understand what can be improved and try to make it available," he explained.

Fabregas also touched upon the necessity of managing stars like Nico Paz, who was rested following a heavy international and European workload. The manager insisted that rotation is a non-negotiable part of the process for a young team trying to establish themselves as a force in both domestic and continental competitions.

"I think it's a great challenge, especially after the Champions League. Coming here with so many changes and this performance, especially in the second half. We didn't leave anything to them, to play or have opportunities. There are moments during the season that we have to manage like this. This is a process of adaptation, we are very young and for me today the reaction was important. I liked the team very much," Fabregas concluded.
